To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
campaign advertising influences political discussion, which in turn influences political participation.

exposure to campaign advertising on television, especially ads that are negative, has a small but significant effect on civic participation, and that the effect of campaign advertising on political participation is indirect and mediated by online news use.

(a) exposure to campaign advertising on television is positively associated with online news consumption, which, in turn, promotes political discussion and participation; and (b) campaign advertising exposure that emphasizes attack messages indirectly and weakly depresses civic and political participation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how campaign advertising influences the use of traditional and new media and, in turn, political discussion and participation.
the effects of political communication on political and civic participation and the mediating role of online political news consumption.
the effects of campaign advertising on political communication processes and civic and political life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
political advertising is an important part of a complex system of campaign communication and political participation, but that it is only one component of this system.
the communication mediation model of campaign effects, as we have specified it, holds up well.
political advertising is a significant factor in shaping the flow of information and the nature of political discussion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

campaign ads, online news consumption, and online political discussion all have important effects on civic and campaign participation, and these effects are mediated by a complex set of relationships that are not easily predicted by the extant literature.
campaign advertising is not a panacea for civic engagement, but it is a necessary component of the communication ecology of civic and campaign life.
campaign advertising is a powerful force in shaping civic and political participation in ways that complement, rather than compete with, traditional media and interpersonal communication channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the campaign communication environment is not simply a ‘‘mediator’’ between the campaign and its audience.

campaign advertising can have a positive impact on civic and political participation, especially if it is used to inform the public about issues and candidates rather than to attack political opponents.
campaign messages can have a positive effect on political engagement, but only when these messages are not too partisan or negative.
